newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: German heating oil use seen falling 2-3 pct per yr.
newsitem.headline: German heating oil use seen falling 2-3 pct per yr.

text.p: Heating oil consumption in Europe's largest market, Germany, is expected to fall by two to three percent per year to 2000, according to a report by the Hamburg-based German Oil Industry Association.
The fall from an expected 35.9 million tonnes this year is forecast as energy efficiency measures take hold and gas supplants heating oil as the fuel of choice for German households.
Demand this decade has been fairly steady, at around 37 million tonnes.

"Houses with heating oil are steadily increasing over the years, but gas use is rising much faster. Better insulation, ovens and general energy usage means overall consumption will fall," an association spokesman said.
The association report takes no account of the vagaries of the weather which can clearly boost overall energy consumption and therefore increase the use of heating oil.
The cold 1995/1996 winter led to a 10 percent year-on-year rise to 38.4 million tonnes in 1996. Smaller stock levels also forced consumers to buy in emergency supplies.
The decline of gas oil consumption should continue, albeit at a slower pace, after 2000 when Germans will buy an estimated 33.4 million tonnes.
In 2005, demand is forecast to be 30.8 million tonnes and, in 2010, 28.3 million tonnes.
"Demand is seen falling by a quarter to 28 million tonnes by the year 2010," the association said.

In the same period, the number of households using heating oil is expected to rise from the current 12.2 million to between 12.5 and 13.3 million in the year 2010. However, the number of households using gas will rise faster.
While demand for heating oil falls, that for diesel will increase.
However, the extra 1.3 million tonnes of consumption forecast for the year 2000 will only partly offset the fall of heating oil demand. It is also not expected to rise in the 10 years to 2010.
